title: Tax‐Avoidance Activities of U.S. Multinational Corporations*

models.model_label: Broad-sample worldwide ETR regression, equation (2), Table 4 column (2)
models.sample_description: U.S.-incorporated Compustat firm-year observations for 1990–97, including multinational and U.S. domestic-only companies. Table 4 reports 16,750 firm-year observations for equation (2). The sample-selection section separately reports a final ETR-analysis pool of 19,737 firm-years (5,379 firms), after exclusions for foreign incorporation, zero ratio denominators, negative assets or stockholders’ equity, missing ETR data, banking/insurance/utilities, nonpositive pre-tax income or total income tax expense, and the top/bottom 1% of return on assets. The paper does not explain why the equation (2) count is lower than that overall ETR-analysis count.
models.method_details: The author states that equations (1)–(4) are estimated using OLS, and identifies Table 4 as OLS results.

review_notes: Table 4 reports 16,750 firm-year observations for equation (2), while the ETR sample-selection section reports 19,737 observations available for ETR analysis. The paper does not explain the lower equation-specific count; its exact reported fit N is retained without inferring the cause.

The supplied reading text renders greater-than signs in the Table 1 MNC rule and multiplication signs in the interaction definitions as hyphens. The original physical PDF page 11 was visually inspected and shows FORPTI > 0, FOROPER > 0, MNC × PTI, and MNC × SIZE; the literal reading-text quotations are retained.

result_sets.horizon: Contemporaneous firm-year worldwide current ETR; SIZE, PTI and foreign-operation terms are measured at the firm-year level.
result_sets.population: U.S.-incorporated Compustat firm-year observations including multinational and U.S. domestic-only companies; Table 4 column (2) reports N=16,750. The ETR sample-selection section separately reports N=19,737, and the paper does not explain the equation-specific difference.
review_notes: Only equation (2), Table 4 column (2) is extracted. Column (1) and Tables 5–6 are outside the selected baseline result set.

Coefficient estimates and t-statistics are transcribed from the selected column. No standard errors or exact p-values are printed; any supported standard-error derivation is performed by the frozen script, while p-value inversion is blocked by unknown sidedness/df.
The table reports location coefficients but suppresses industry and year dummy coefficients; those absences are recorded in model results.missing_fields.
Adjusted R² is a fit statistic and is not included as a parameter or descriptive variable.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
Sample selection
Table 2 summarizes the sample selection procedures. I obtained all firm-year
observations with the requisite data on COMPUSTAT for 1990–97, resulting in
52,125 total observations. Since tax planning by foreign corporations may be systematically different from the tax planning by U.S. corporations, I deleted foreign
incorporated firms from the initial sample (2,249 firm-year observations). I also
deleted observations with zero values in the denominator of a ratio (3,885 firmyears), observations with negative assets or stockholder’s equity (3,820 firm-years),
and observations with missing ETR data (122 firm-years). I deleted banks, insurance

Previous ETR studies (Stickney and McGee 1982; Zimmerman 1983; Wilkie
1988; Shevlin and Porter 1992; Wilkie and Limberg 1993; Manzon and Smith
1994; Gupta and Newberry 1997) have deleted firms with negative tax expense or
negative pre-tax income. Loss firms have different financial and tax-reporting
incentives and ETRs with negative components do not have an economic interpretation. To be consistent with prior research, I have also deleted firm-year observations
with income tax expense or pre-tax income less than or equal to zero (17,271 firmyears). <sup>15</sup>

Finally, I performed two actions to eliminate the effects of extreme values.
First, ETRs greater than one were recoded as one (405 firm-years). Second, I
deleted observations (410 firm-years) if they were in the top or bottom 1 percent of
the return on assets distribution. The final sample is 19,737 firm-year observations
(5,379 firms). <sup>16</sup>
